target_customer: Consumers in India who pay a small fee per check at public kiosks, plus corporate and institutional sponsors of the machines
problem: Few people in India get routine screening for non communicable disease risk factors such as obesity and hypertension, and clinic visits are a barrier.
business_model: Pay per use health check kiosks in public places (basic checks from INR 50 per the company's 2020 release), with potential sponsorship and data services

founders.name: Joginder Tanikella
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as a hands-on CEO and full-stack developer in software and embedded systems. No education or prior employers found in sources opened.

technical_complexity.rationale: Combined sensors for BMI, body composition, blood pressure and glucose into a networked kiosk manufactured in India, which needs hardware, embedded software and a reporting app; sensor integration is standard but hardware at small scale is harder than software.

defensibility.rationale: Kiosk hardware built from off the shelf sensors can be copied; the main advantage is placement in public locations (150 locations in 106 cities by March 2020) and accumulated check data.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Indian Railways launched Health ATM kiosks sponsored by other operators such as Yolo Health in late 2019, showing rivals entered the same locations; no incumbent acquired the company in sources found.

market_need_then: India had a large burden of non communicable disease and low screening rates; the company cited mass screening as the gap. Demand evidence is the company's own reported 450,000 checks by March 2020 and 600,000 by the YC page.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and mission led: preventive health for everyone

branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage at the Bio Asia 2023 summit described the machine as making checkups fun, but no community or merch evidence was found.

brand_strength.rationale: Pulse is a very common name used by many unrelated companies, and the legal entity is named Quantificare Health Stations, so search results are confused; no sourced brand assets beyond the machine itself.

outcome_analysis: The company is still listed as active, has a strategic investment from ASICS Ventures in March 2020 and reports hundreds of thousands of checks, but no large round is verified. Rivals entered public locations such as railway stations in late 2019. Its path as a small hardware kiosk network looks slow rather than failed, and the funding record is too thin to call it a success or a stall.
notes: Company website returned HTTP 503 when fetched. Aggregators (CB Insights, Seedtable, Bouncewatch) report about $150K total and a 2019 pre-seed and a 2021 round led by TheVentures; these figures come from aggregators only and conflict, so they are unverified and not recorded as rounds. The amount of the ASICS investment is not disclosed. Another outlet reports the company as largely bootstrapped. Legal name Quantificare Health Stations Pvt Ltd per search snippets. No competitor with a source dated at or before the 2019 batch was found; Indian Railways Health ATM kiosks date to late 2019 and are later entrants. The outcome search found no acquisition, shutdown or layoff news.
